prompt2:
A string S is given.
Find how many places in S have A, B, and C in this order.
Specifically, find triples of integers (i,j,k) that satisfy all of the following conditions. Here, |S| denotes the length of S, and S_x denotes the x-th character of S.
- 1 \leq i < j < k \leq |S|
- j - i = k - j
- S_i = A
- S_j = B
- S_k = C
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
S
Output
Print the result.
Constraints
- S is an uppercase English string with length between 3 and 100, inclusive.

Clarification: Print only the number of such triples as an integer; if the count is zero, print 0.

Clarification: Yes, if |S|=3 and S_1='A', S_2='B', S_3='C', then it counts as one triple.
